texts.text: <color=#515aee>Here... Kindness and valor will shine...</color>
Ah... At last, to be graced with the sweet release from the gaol that was the restroom...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Still, I'm glad it was at least a well-appointed restroom.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Even though the ethereally mysterious lady never spoke to the rest of us the whole time.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Verily! 'Twas quite admirable, her reticence! I, for one, could never have contained myself...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: To hold back the words that yearn to be spoken, to still the body that desires to fidget, is to invite a horrible itchiness to plague the pits of my belly and the tips of my toes!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Fuhu, I've just the cure for that. When you need to stay still, just close your eyes and... think of something you really like. You'll feel your breathing slow down as your mind finds peace.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Close my eyes and... think of something I really like...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ...! The Grass Maiden! I conjure in my mind the Grass Maiden's newest ultimate move...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Ah, how graceful she is! How fiercely beautiful the roundhouse kick pirouettes...! Ooh... should fortune permit, I shall demonstrate a recreation of her magnificence before ye!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: And so you will, once we get back to the restroom. Fuhu...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Very well, young Hong Lu! Thou hast bestowed upon me a relaxation technique most wondrous indeed.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <... What relaxation technique?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ooooh... 'Tis as though we have walked through a portal into another world.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Do you like it? Rocinante must be happy to find so many friends here.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Alas! Harbor no fear, dearest Rocinante... For I am not so vain a horsemaster that I would abandon a loyal steed such as thee for the first new mount that seizeth mine eye.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Nay, not at all... I would never...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Lean any closer, and you might end up eating the shoe, Don Quixote.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Ahem, 'tis but a close inspection, nothing more...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: What a disgrace you are, Four-legs. You were entrusted with but one duty—one—the shop's cleanliness. Yet I see that you've failed spectacularly at that simple task.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: I have indeed failed you, honorable One-leg. I couldn't carry out that simple duty on account of my stupidity and idleness.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: There is a reason you are made to drag those unsightly legs with you, Four-legs. Remind yourself of that with every step you take.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: ... I understand, One-leg. My deepest apologies.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Forgive that shameful display, dear customer. Lowly though I am, I will now attend to you instead. ... Should you tolerate my vulgar presence, of course.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Is... is all well? That one-legged woman seemed to be bullying thee quite harshly.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: In the sartorial arts, a shoe is an article of clothing wrought to meet the ground and spare the body from the impurities of dirt. The fewer the feet that touch the ground, the nobler the being—and the more exalted the purpose of the lone shoe.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: As our names suggest, lowly Four-legs like myself walk the earth with too many appendages...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: The universal aspiration of the Footwear Hall employees is to ascend into a higher state of being—"One-leg," whose sheer existence is balanced proudly upon a single leg.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: W-well... If thou sayest so... Then what must one do to become a... "One-leg"?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Craft shoes with tireless devotion. Sell them in faithfulness. Discipline the body so that fewer and fewer feet may tread upon the ground. Perseverance and persistence shall be our salvation—
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: —and once we have become worthy, the shoes shall transfigure us.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: You must all be quite new to this floor, if you're still asking questions like that.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Yes, we are. We came up from the floors below.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: From the— You're from downstairs...? Then might you be the customers everyone is whispering about...? The customers who are unbound to the floors...?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Mm. We can travel between floors without restriction.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Verily, I must wonder: how doth such rumor spread, when travel betwixt each floor is restricted for most inhabitants of the Grand Magasin?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Little birds aren't bound by height, it seems.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I... see. The rumors were true. Only rumors are allowed to travel between each floor of this department store, so we never know whether they're true or false.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Then... could you confirm the veracity of another rumor for me?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Hm, what rumor would that be?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: It used to be that the customers of the Grand Magasin who collapsed could rise again on the lower floors. However many times they collapsed, they could begin anew from the very start.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Yet ever since the day the cracks formed on the walls... I hear that collapsed customers no longer rise—not just here, but on the lower floors, too.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Is there any... grain of truth to that?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: It is true. Revival is no longer possible here.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Then the rumor was true.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Even if we collapse, we will never again awaken on B1 as we always did...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: I've always had so much admiration for the One-legs... and their magnificent stance as they pushed themselves against the earth with but the strength of a single leg, the whole of their existence concentrated upon a singular point. But it was always out of my reach, no matter how hard I labored.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Each time I woke anew on B1, I endured in the hope that this life—this one—might be the one where I am granted the honor of joining the One-legs.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: But there's no "next time" anymore... is there?
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: If there is no next time... I'll never brave losing my legs. Not without the ability to reawaken and start over from the first floor.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: I will remain arrested by these appendages. A wretched, worthless Four-legs, left to crawl through the Grand Magasin for all eternity.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: Pray, do not demean thyself so! Whether thy legs number four or one, what concern is it to thee? 'Tis of no import—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: You'd never understand... You're not the one stuck forever in the Footwear Hall.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: I've a request. If you will grant me that mercy.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: I am wretched and worthless... And now... only one way remains... by which I may cease to be a Four-legs.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: You can collapse me, can't you? You're all strong and prestigious enough to move between floors.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: When you do... cut off my legs... These useless... hideous legs...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: ... Thine wish is to be free of all four appendages?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Yes. All of my legs.
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: But—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Instead of waiting to hear our reply, the Four-legs lunged at us... with an approximation of a contented smile on his face.
Aaah... At long last...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: So this is how emancipating it feels, to be... deprived of legs...
texts.speaker: Four-legs

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>No matter how much they'd lost, no matter how far they'd fallen, the inhabitants of the Grand Magasin could always begin anew from rock bottom.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Equal opportunity for everyone, no matter how lowly their status is, or how badly they'd failed.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>... Not anymore, though.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>And that's all thanks to you, Meursault.</color>
You are blaming me for my mother's death.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Of course I am. Who else would I blame but her murderer?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>We Giants each play an indispensable role as the pillars that uphold Sisyphe. And your mother was one of us.</color>
I don't suppose this warrants repeating, ma puce, but N Corp. was determined to give you the Sisyphe Penalty right away. You do know the lengths I went to stop that... don't you?
I do. I remember everything.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>But did you thank me? No. You don't seem all that grateful now, either.</color>
I do not recall asking for your help.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>The... vacancy left behind by your mother changed the Grand Magasin in more ways than one.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>One, the fractures that appeared on its walls. It plunged the Grand Magasin and its inhabitants into chaos and confusion.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>So, we procured this "Golden Bough" and planted it in the very same seat where she used to work. A stopgap, if you will. The position of a Giant that shoulders Sisyphe's weight requires a very particular set of specifications, and we didn't know when the next candidate would appear.</color>
The Golden Bough...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <She must be talking about the events that occurred outside the Grand Magasin.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: And that's what caused the so-called "Golden Resin" to appear and fill the fractures...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Correct.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>Some called that mending gold a "hide," while it was "resin" to others. Regardless of the disagreements over its proper denomination, however, the Voice began speaking to everyone from within its golden light.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Ever since that whisper filled this place... the Noirs succumbed to fear, while the Rouges began sniffing out opportunity.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Two...</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Death became final. Those who died in the Grand Magasin Sisyphe could no longer come back to life.</color>

<color=#ebcaa2>This puts N Corp. in a rather unenviable position, as the irreversibility of death means that their stock of raw ingredients for Canned Experience production will inevitably run out unless they're replenished "manually."</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Which is exactly what they've been doing by passing the Sisyphe Penalty with ever greater frequency.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Meanwhile, we three remaining Giants are forced to strain ourselves all the harder to keep this place aloft.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>And maybe that's where you can come in, ma puce. You have just the required set of skills to fill your mother's vacancy, don't you?</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>I've always wondered why you never bothered to tell them that right off the bat. You've always known that you have what it takes to become a Giant.</color>
... There was no reason to tell them that. My aptitude for the position had no bearing on the fact that I did kill Mother.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#ebcaa2>Well, in light of what has happened since then, you might want to reconsider that stance.</color>
<color=#ebcaa2>Unless you're starting to find life in the Grand Magasin increasingly attractive, that is.</color>
With that, Jeanne fell silent once again.
... So, according to Miss Jeanne... the Golden Bough is the last thing holding the Grand Magasin together.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Then... what would happen to this place if we removed it?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hm... Verily, the "resin" sealing the fissures would disappear... whereupon the collapse of the department store would surely follow...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hoh... Would not the liberation of incarcerated N Corp. residents be within reach, then?! 'Twould be a most fortuitous outcome!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: then think about the consequences.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Now that we know for sure that the Golden Bough isn't inside the Grand Magasin, we can leave this place, pluck it out, and find out.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... A foolish, ignorant death... Perfectly befitting a Four-legs.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: It never understood the natural order that governs the Footwear Hall. The cycle in which the sole purpose of the Four-legs' base existence is to elevate us One-legs to be revered.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: And you—insolent strangers. You dare flout the rules of this domain with such impunity?
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <This is somehow becoming our fault...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I have no shoes to sell to strangers such as yourselves. Nor do I recall ever permitting your presence in this hall.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Refuse to remove yourselves from the premises, and... I will displace you all personally.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <I don't like where this is going... Let's show her the Authenticity Certificate we received downstairs before things get out of control.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The Noirs on the third floor gave us this.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Le Noir Authenticity Certificate...
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: ... As a One-leg, I normally don't deal with customers of your... bipedal standing. But it is true that no average Two-legs carries an Authenticity Certificate as you do...
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Very well, I'll make an exception just this once.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <First, let's explain what happened on the third floor.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Meursault brought the One-leg up to speed with the events of the third floor.
Ooho... What a thrilling adventure thou hast had, Manager Esquire!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The Rouges, bereft of their Voice, hmm?
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: I doubted that rumor at first, but... this may as well be a confirmation.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: No wonder they've been sneaking between the floors. They're clearly scheming something untoward... Everything clicks.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Scheming?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: See, we had this policy of turning every Rouge we encountered into an insole. Their avarice makes them exceptionally tough—few materials provide a shoe with stronger padding, you see.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Every time we caught one of them, they had the same thing to say to us.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: That a new Voice shall soon come to whisper in their ears, and that its first utterance would usher in an age of ruin eternal.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: We never took them seriously, of course, but what you have recounted lends some merit to their words. After all, they've lost their guiding Voice—cornered animals will stoop to anything, you know.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: The present conundrum is, however... that we do not know where in the Grand Magasin they could be scheming.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <Wait, I've only made a brief stop there, but when we visited the second floor...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... they said they were undergoing... "renovations." And there were bodies of Le Noir employees behind them.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes, there was indeed a massacre underway on the second floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: That's where the Luxury Hall is located. So they've made a nest of that place, did they? All in service of their preposterous plan of birthing a new Voice...
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Two-legs. Would you say that you are allies of Le Noir?
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <That's... how it turned out, I guess?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: They're saying "yes"~
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: You're all able to move between floors without obstruction... strangers such as yourselves should make for perfect messengers for us Noirs.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: ... Very well, then. We'll let you purchase shoes from our shop.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Under one condition, however.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Should you come across any information that may be of assistance to the Noirs, you come to us right away.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Pray, what sort of intelligence wouldst thou deem to be of assistance?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Let me give you some pointers, though it may be but an old tale from quite a few seasons ago. The Kakis who make their home in the Furniture Hall stole a few items from us Noirs.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: We didn't bother pursuing them, as those items had already passed out of fashion by then. However... among the items they thieved was an artifact said to be a most precious weapon—it's said that all fabric is as delicate as gauze before its might.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Ooh, a legendary artifact the likes of which are heard only from tales of heroics...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: If such a weapon does exist, I'm sure it will be of great assistance to us in our war against the Rouges. The fabric used to create the Rouges' clothes—made from an unholy amalgamation of the Golden Resin and all kinds of hedonistic desires—is rather difficult for us to tear apart.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <Okay, then. Let's hand it over... if we ever do come across it.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <With that done, why don't we look around for more stuff on this floor?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What might this place be...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Looks like they sell furniture here.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <This hall is especially quiet....>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Verily, 'tis a hall most spacious yet tranquil!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Yes, like most furniture and home decor shops.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Th-this be a lamp, or this be a man? Forsooth, a pickle indeed...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hmm... that sure is a conundrum. Wouldn't that depend on how we look at it?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: You need only consider every entity here a customer, a product, a vendor, and a Mannequin all at once.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ah, insooth...! Then perchance I can prod this gentlelamp for the ins-and-outs of this hall most puzzling!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Hark, kind Sir!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Aha. Customers.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Will you... Will you purchase me?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Though my bent back may give you an impression of bad posture at first, it is in fact my strength—the subtle combination of height and angle ensures that any customer in search of respite will be most appropriately illuminated.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Ah, well. In truth, w-what we seek is—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I may creak a little—the last customer who inspected me was regrettably coarse with their hands. But worry you not. My functions are not one bit affected.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Come, feel the softness of my body. Why don't you try lighting me up now, young fellows?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: N-nay, worry thee not. In truth, 'tis simply that thou were the first to catch mine eye—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Caught your eye, did I?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Well, well, well... Isn't that encouraging to hear? It can only mean that I am clearly different in terms of composition compared to the rest of the common rabble on display here!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Perchance, that may be so. 'Tis quite blindingly bright where thou standest, indeed.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: is a lamp...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Someone with such a keen eye for aesthetic detail will surely be willing to purchase me, hmm?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I am yours for a very reasonable price of 4,000 eyeballs. Outrageously underpriced for the unmatched coziness my lighting provides, if I do say so myself.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: <Outrageously overpriced, you mean!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: A-ah, 'tis clear now that there hath been a misunderstanding of sorts 'twixt us! We were not of mind to purchase thee—or any light, for that matter—our eyes have not yet dimmed so woefully as to require one.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... So, you were just window shopping after all.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Perhaps another time~
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Curses... Foiled once again...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: It was entirely unnecessary of you to remind me of my appearance... Though by a stroke of errant fortune I was willed to move again, spurred on by the warmth of this brilliant sunlight peering through the cracks of the Grand Magasin, my long slumber has left my leather worn and saggy...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: ... Ah, I've got it. If I were to procure an incredibly dashing outfit to complement my appearance... Hmm... Yes, I'll make the sale in no time.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: That's it. Dear customers, I now make you an offer of a lifetime. Bring me the most fashionable and suitable outfit for me from the Furniture Hall owner, and in return...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: ... I will give you a most generous 2.5% discount and make myself available at an even more reasonable price of 3,900 eyeballs. I'm willing to bet you haven't been graced with a deal this good in your entire lives—not only am I dressed in a stylish outfit, but I'm yours for a price that is practically a steal!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: nothing to convince me to buy this guy. And 3,900 eyeballs is still an outrageous asking price... just not in the way he thinks.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh, but this gives us an excuse to pay a visit to the owner of this Hall.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Aha!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Established patterns suggest that initiating a conversation with someone in the managerial position of each hall will most likely lead to discovering the means to access the next floor, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Content!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Very well, we shall be there and back again anon!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... H-AAAAARK!! Be thou the master of this hall?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: H-hark...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Excuse me~ We're here because Mister Lamp over there told me that you'd show us some outfits for him?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I wonder if they're unable to speak?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: (There is no reply. For lack of a better word, the figure "unfurls" its body, displaying an assortment of miscellany... including what appear to be parts of the human anatomy.)
Hoh... Could this be... thy manner of parley? Ah, I see! Thou'rt flaunting thy colección, perchance?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: (Still, there is no reply. The figure stands in silence, quietly dangling the collection of various unrecognizable—and some, regrettably recognizable—miscellany from its body.)
Or... maybe they're asking us to take them with us.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Could you confirm if that's what you're trying to communicate, owner of the Furniture Hall?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: (The owner does not so much as twitch.)
<... Okay, then. We'll pick something that'll look good on the Lamp and leave?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: (We take an item from their body, but they still don't stir. Only when we've walked a fair distance away from them do they fold themselves shut.)
Erm...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Behold! 'Tis the artifact of our choice—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I must say... this piece is not entirely consonant with my own aesthetic sense...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Ack!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... However, as you are all doubtlessly true aesthetes who have managed to recognize my overwhelming magnificence within the Furniture Hall... I trust that there was some apocryphal philosophy behind this choice of fashion. I will... wear it, I guess...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: But you can forget about my most generous discount offer. Frankly, your choice of outfit has been nothing but disappointment to me...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Oh, in that case, in exchange for rescinding your discount offer...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... would you mind answering a few simple questions for us?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Why, of course. The magnanimity of my heart is every bit as warm as my ivory-white bulb. Do speak.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: So, about the owner—
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: AH! And in my infinite wisdom, which can be inferred from the most graceful shape of my lampshade and its complex deco, I have already deduced the nature of your question before it has even left your lips.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: We call the owner... the "Happy Closet."
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Yes. They are truly a giving soul—so willing to part with pretty much anything inside their body! And why "Happy", you ask? Well... They have never once complained about it, and therefore I must imagine they are quite happy. Presumably.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: And why... do you think they're like that?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: How should I know? We've been sitting here gathering dust for ages... It is simply what it means to be a piece of Furnishing.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Then... wherefore hast thou chosen to become as Furnishings?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... Because we've all chosen to linger...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: We have long come to terms with the fact that we will never be able to reach the top floor... Or gain entry to the Luxury Hall to shop there...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Then is it not wiser to wait in stillness upon this floor and sleep the days away until some wealthy soul chooses to purchase us...?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: <Then why did he wake up, all of a sudden?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What was it that caused you to awaken from your sleep all of a sudden?
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Well, that's... I don't know when it began, but a warm ray of the sun shone its light on me.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Stirred awake by that light, I pushed myself off the ground, and... the Happy Closet opened themselves up to us.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Do you know what excruciating torture it is to be awake? It is agony without respite.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Oh, how I wish someone would purchase me... I just want to sleep... in affluence...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Which leads me to my next point: has my offer become any more attractive? See, even with a layer of the outfit you've brought me, I am still available for a low, low price of 4,000 eyeballs! This is an outrageous price for what I bring to the table, dear customers!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: NO! Buy me, buy me!
Gah!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: You gave that rusty old lamp an outfit?! No fair, he's been outta fashion since forever, dudes! Do me too, do me too! Decorate me!
Dress me up, and I'll let you buy me at an affordable price!
He has it so good. Hardly any sunlight reaches us back here... Let us have something, too...

If you won't, then we'll...
If you won't, then we'll...
<I don't like where this is going...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I-is it just me, or hath this hall become much more... frigid...?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <And the owner of this hall can't even explain any of this to us, let alone speak at all...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <We're going to have to do as those Furnishings ask if we want even a snowball's chance in hell of figuring things out.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: (The Happy Closet, as the others called them, opens up to us once again.)
texts.speaker: Happy Closet

texts.text: So... I wonder what the other Furnishings are looking for?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hm... It shall be of our choosing. Good Closet, wouldst thou allow us to take several at once from thee?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: (The Happy Closet still does not stir.)
texts.speaker: Happy Closet

texts.text: <I... guess they don't mind...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text:
So slow!
So slow!
<Okay, then... I guess we're taking everything from this side?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What took you so long?! My bones're freezing from the lack of deco!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: A-apologies, good fellow, What is it that thou needst?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: I want a toenail! Toenail on my hat! I'll look so classy with a toenail on my hat!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Toenail... This be the toenail thou seekest, perchance?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Heavens... Have you misplaced your eyes on the soles of your feet?! Try putting them where you can see!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: This looks like a toenail to you? It's obviously a tongue!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Ah...! Had I not shared much the same doubt with thee, Manager Esquire? Loath I be to say it, but thou truly hast no eye for the aesthetics of fashion!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: But... this is a pretty nice tongue, I'll give you that. It'll go quite well with my light.
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: Oh boy, hope I'll sell for a high price...
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: *yawn* So sleepy...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Why do I gotta stay awake...?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Hello, what outfit would you like?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I mean, it's obvious, isn't it...? Something beautiful so someone'll buy me soon... Ah, I know... I want a warm and fuzzy coat, so I can snooze right back to sleep as soon as I'm sold...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Sure thing, here you go—
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... What do you want me to do with this? Drape it over me.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: You think I should be bothered to haul myself up to get dressed? Do you have any idea how sleepy I am?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: <... Is this bed serious?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh, haha... Here you go. How's that?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: So nice... So nice. You can go.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: I'm gonna need some time to get used to this fuzzy coziness... I'll... uhm... give you a discount of 200 eyeballs when I'm fully acclimated. A token of my gratitude.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: You better purchase me, okay?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: I like that you're bringing me the good stuff willingly, my dudes.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: You guys must be the totally kewl~ kinda customers.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Thank you for your kind words. Here—which one would you like?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Guess what? I'm a totally kewl~ Furnishing, too. Yoink! Didn't even need to think.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: <Didn't even hesitate, huh...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: With that done, why don'tcha dudes be totally kewl~ too and buy me?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I'll give ya a discount of 300 eyeballs if you're kewl~ about it, how's that, my dudes?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I ask thee, in a manner most kewl~—what be thy price, with that most generous discount?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: It makes me a totes reasonable 3,600 eyeballs. Far out, huh? Oops, or am I lowballing myself?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Silence descended around us as we all struggled to come to terms with that ridiculous asking price.
Dang, not so kewl~ after all, huh?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: That's gonna be a no-go for me, my dudes. I want my buyer to be totally kewl~.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Really? This is all that's left inside the Closet?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Hmm... Kinda disappointing, guys.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Why didn't you come to me first before anyone else?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: We weren't avoiding you, if that's what you're saying. We just happened to visit everyone here in the order they caught our eye...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: *scoff* Are you implying that I'm not as eye-catching as the others?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Hmph! I know I'm on the somewhat petite side in this Hall, but there's no need to be so rude.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Forget it, I'm taking this.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: And don't think you'll be getting a good-bye OR a thank-you discount from me!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: That's too bad, then. We won't be able to afford you without a discount.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: ... Hmph.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: S-see if I care! I bet someone way, way richer than you'll splurge for me soon!
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Thank you... Thank you ever so much for bringing me such a precious item.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: <Wow, a polite Distor—I mean, Furnishing for once.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I hope this isn't an imposition, but... Oh, every garment you brought me is simply beautiful... I'll go with this one.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Mm.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: And this one...
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Aaaaand this one.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: One item per customer.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Ah, really?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: Oh... I'm sorry, I must've gotten ahead of myself. The sunshine's been so warm lately, I feel like I'm floating.
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: But don't you think it's rather heartless of you to throw me one miserable scrap of sacking and expect me to go over the rainbow?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: It's our policy.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Tsk. That's a stupid fucking policy, isn't it?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text: <... Whoa. That's a switch-up for sure.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The fuck're you lookin' at! Get lost, fuckwit!
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text:
Me this one!
This one!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Mm.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text:
Wow!
Wow!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
Thankies!
Thankies!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: <Glad that was easy, at least.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text:
Wanna buy me?
Buy me!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
9,900 eyeballs! A steal!
A steal!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Thine offer is the most exorbitant price we have heretofore encountered!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text:
Yep, yep!
Yep, yep!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
Cuz I'm awesome!
I'm awesome!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: Alas, we have not with us such a grand sum of—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text:
What a bum!
What a bum!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: How cruel of thee...!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Don't take it too personally, Don Quixote. We are a bit strapped for eyeballs at the moment.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: I thank thy generosity, kind Closet! Thou hast been indispensable in dressing the other Furnishings with outfits most fashionable.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: (The Happy Closet opens up without a word.)
texts.speaker: Happy Closet

texts.text: <Why are they opening up again?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Maybe it's their way of saying that... it's okay for us to take more?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Perchance... Yet, I must ask thee: wherefore wouldst thou so charitably make thy possessions available to us gratis?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: We know not whether these be their hoarded treasure, akin to a precious colección of limited-time releases...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: If you were in the same situation, would you willingly give up your collection of badges to help the people in need?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Mmm... If it be in service of helping the troubled, then I shall fain part with my entire colección—!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: —eeeeeeeehhhhhhhhh, though, mayhap thou wilt be merciful and spare the limited edition Red Mist commemorative badge? 'Twould leave me with naught but sorrow were I to be deprived of even that...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Oh, stop it with your pearl-clutching.
W-what is the meaning of this? A-and... ye were all mobile, all along?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: *yawn* Tried to get some shut-eye... but the sunshine kept me up.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: I'm going to need more than one article of clothing if I want someone to buy me before the sunshine grows even warmer.
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Bet that closet's hiding even kewl~er goodies inside.
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: I bet they've got some luxury stuff hidden inside that you uncultured swines couldn't even recognize.
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: I hope this isn't an imposition, but would you mind giving me everything you have?
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text:
Want all of it!
All of it!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: W-wait, what—?!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Move, move! Me first pick! Me first pick!!
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: ... As we reel from the sudden turn of events, the Furnishings shove us aside and descend upon the motionless Happy Closet like a flock of carrion birds.
Their body remains unfurled even as they are knocked down to the ground.
*yawn*... Shame, Rocking Chair sold for 2,100 eyeballs. Would've been me had they not been wearing that newfangled scarf. Now they'll get to sleep forever—must be so, so very nice...
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Keep dreaming, you greedy thing. You took the most clothes out of Happy Closet, you know?
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text: Hope there's a cow-print shin somewhere in there... That'd be pretty kewl~ ya know?
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: You bitch, that lower lip you just took is pretty much a set with the philtrum I chose!
texts.speaker: Skinhide Couch

texts.text:
Leave the eyebrows!
Leave the eyebrows!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: <... They could've all just moved on their own.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Those scoundrels were much like a pack of bandits descending upon a hapless victim... 'Tis not right, though the Happy Closet be a giving soul.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Whether it is right or wrong is of no significance.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What—!
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The concepts of right and wrong are contingent on the perspective of the observer, and are therefore shallow and muddled.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Excuse me.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Oh? Hello, Mister Lamp. When did you...?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: You can get out of my way if you have no further business with the closet.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Uh...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: What brazen sabotage... Looking to snatch away my potential customers, eh? I won't take it sitting down!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: <As if the Happy Closet was his to begin with, huh...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Drat it... Just as I feared. They nabbed everything but the skin of the face... This simply won't do. It's a wretchedly difficult article to coordinate into an outfit set...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Wait, there's one thing left...!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: The heart...! The heart remains...!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Yes, that's the most priceless article out of them all. Were I to wear the heart...!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Oh, I'll be worth 10,000 eyeballs... or even more!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I'll finally have an owner...!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: W-well, so who gets to claim the heart?
texts.speaker: Mellow Leather Bed

texts.text: Look, there's mold growing on my body... I gotta sell before it spreads all over me...
texts.speaker: Taxidermied Leather Curtain

texts.text: Then... let us divide it equally amongst us.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: O Happy Closet, I have but one humble request for you... Could you, by any chance... part with your heart for our sake...?
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: That heart of yours shall surely elevate us to the coveted state of ownership...
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Capital! That's a yes. Well then, don't mind me if I do.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Precision, please! Okay?
texts.speaker: Bonehanger

texts.text: You better slice it into three equal, identical parts...
texts.speaker: Red-cushioned Stool

texts.text:
Ooh, heart!
Ooh, heart!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text:
Mine!
Mine!
texts.speaker: Lamp Twin

texts.text: As I watched the carnage and plunder in horror, the world before me lurched and changed—as though an unseen hand had spliced the scene away.
Are these Meursault's memories...? But I don't see him anywhere in them.
<Wait, these aren't... These aren't Meursault's memories...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <So that's... Jeanne...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Is it the role of these "Giants" to... observe the Grand Magasin from outside?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The Furnishings, and everyone whom we had encountered thus far, were they not all once—
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... "normal humans of the City?" was perhaps what she'd intended to say. But she let her words trail off, the rest of her thoughts unspoken.
Correct. That is one of the responsibilities assigned to the Giants.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then, pray—would one be correct in assuming that the role of a Giant is given to those who revel in the suffering of others?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: No. It is the opposite.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The opposite?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: The Giants are all...
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... those who are afraid.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Afraid? What are they afraid of?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: All of it.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: At first glance, the room resembles an ordinary cinema. It is a dark and quiet place, insulated from even the smallest noise beyond its walls.
Like any other cinema, there are seats. On each of them are people, sitting in rows upon rows of idleness, their eyes uniformly fixed on the large screen at the end of the theater room.
Only the sounds of consumption sliding down the gullets break through the silence.
The following words are projected onto the screen: "Canned Film - Title: A Lone Fixer Departs into the Sunset".
The image is static.
Its stasis is in contrast to the audience, who consume—some with straws, some with spoons—from the cans that can be eaten only within this cinema.
And yet, each member of the audience sees something different shifting in the shadows. Different moments. Different lives. Different experiences.
I focus on two people in the audience. They are leaning into each other as any loving couple would, so closely that their shoulders touch.
... I wonder if we're both feeling the same thing.
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: I'm afraid. Even now, when we're pressed so close together.
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: We're eating from the same Canned Experience—the view of the sunset. But... can we really say that the sun going down over your horizon is the same one as mine?
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: I am afraid. I'm afraid of... all of it.
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: Afraid of the sky at this time of day. Afraid of the air, of this sensation on my skin... Afraid of my own liminal existence inside it all.
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: Why am I so frightened?
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: These sensations, these thoughts... they're beyond my control. They germinate, blossom, and burst out of me like a streetcar out of control...
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: ... Why did I have to be born as this creature—a human?
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: You'll never answer that, I know. The City won't either. You'll both hold onto your silences until the end of days.
texts.speaker: Jeanne

texts.text: <... Are you... afraid too, Meursault?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I am, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Was there a specific reason, or...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: It began when we were nearing a year since my mother...
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... had first begun her tearful wailing.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Meursault tinkers with the chain link binding his belt together. Clink.
Then, silence fell around us.
(There's no movement. Only remnants of the pillaging remain.)
texts.speaker: Happy Closet

texts.text: Ah...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Amidst the quiet, we noticed that the Happy Closet... had gone completely still. Only the remnants of the pillaging remained.
Hong Lu leaned in and picked up a small piece of paper from what was left behind.
Hmm...? What's this...?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Rubbish, that's what! I have no need of it.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: I'll generously part with that piece of trash should you like to take it.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Stunned, Don Quixote stared blankly at the closet's remains.
There is something written on the paper, Manager. It may contain information that is worth reading.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <O-oh, yeah. Let's read what it says...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: "All shall be awakened by the Golden Fabric and the Nail; so too shall they lull them all to sleep."
<The Golden Fabric and the Nail, huh...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Could this be the legendary weapon that One-leg mentioned...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That's definitely possible.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: <Well, we did promise to update her if we came across anything important.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... They've...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: ... truly given away everything, haven't they?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: So, such ruin is what awaits those whose generosity is untempered.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Don Quixote's sullen gaze lingered on what was left of the Happy Closet. She unpinned a Fixer badge hidden in her jacket and placed it gently on the floor, next to the Closet's remains.
... Let's go.
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <... Yeah.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh hello, dear customers.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Does anything catch your eye? No? Look around anyway—something might!
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Um... have you given up on selling yourself?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: With so many items draped over me, I'm afraid I may have become a tad unaffordable.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: So I thought perhaps I would do well to sell off some of these useless trinkets.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Since you were of some help to me, I'll make an exception and sell them to you without the markup.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: Don't expect any discounts, of course.
texts.speaker: Arc Floor Lamp

texts.text: We came across this recipe in the Furniture Hall.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: This is... Huh. Can't believe something this precious was in possession of those pathetic Furnishings.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: My decision to ally with you Two-legs is looking better and better.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Perhaps maintaining a degree of connection to the humble and the downtrodden is a virtue, pathetic as your peasantry might be.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <... Did she just call us humble and downtrodden?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Take this to the Noirs on the lower floor.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <Hold on, before we go... Can you ask her if she knows how we can get to the fifth floor?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Excuse me, how do we get to the fifth floor?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: The fifth floor...?
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Only those of exalted nobility may enter that floor, Two-legs. You've first got to be up to parity with their dress code.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: The sheer exclusivity of that floor makes it so that not even I, a One-leg, may enter freely. Though my singular footwear be of unparalleled beauty, the rest of my outfit must be up to its stringent standards as well.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Th-then what is it that we must do?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: Wear something more... exceptional, of course. Perhaps something truly premium from a Luxury label, at the very least.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: <Luxury label? Sounds like something from the Luxury Hall on the second floor...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That Hall was not in any condition to be open for business.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The only task I have for you at the moment, lowly plebeians, is to bring this note to the Noirs on the lower floor.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: Not to say that it is a trivial task, no. You're special customers carrying a special missive from the illustrious and elevated One-leg—the outcome shall be just as outstanding, I'm sure.
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: If it be so elevated, then how is it that the second floor—whose elevation is, indeed, beneath that of the fourth floor—holds greater prestige than that of the fourth floor, where thou residest?
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: The One-leg stared at us, stumped. I could see all kinds of thoughts and answers and concerns racing through her mind behind those eyes. Then, after a moment that felt like an eternity...
It just is, okay?!
texts.speaker: One-leg

texts.text: The way ahead is completely blocked. It does not seem possible to pass through for now.
Strangely enough, though they won't ever regain the courage to stand up, they look to be more at peace now...
Of the two lamps, the lit one whispers something. Its lampshade silently swings like a pendulum.
Blink.
Blink.
Bliiiiink.
The lamp seems to blink gratefully.
BlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlinkBlink
... Not grateful, got it.

That set something off.
Mere seconds after I laid my hands on the black couch, the distinct shuffling of Furnishings begin creeping up toward us from the shadows.

Probably shouldn't have touched that...
I hear the Furnishings creeping awake and shambling toward us from who knows where.

I wipe off a thick layer of dust that has settled on the black couch.
Furnishings of all kinds creak to life from all around us... and begin to creep in our direction.
There are a dozen or so legs hanging from the ceiling, all wearing footwear of sorts. A chilling, alien sensation cuts through me.
A display of various shoes.
This display is empty. The label underneath it says [SOLD OUT].
I guess people do shop here...? Empty spots in the display stand out to me.
Black shoes with golden highlights.
Unlike the somber black shoes we've seen so far, these ones are more ostentatious.
This isn't the most apt expression for shoes, but... There's a "canopy" of shoes hanging from the ceiling.
It's like looking up at the ceiling from the floor.
These shoes look pretty elaborate. But... they're at least in the realm of what one might categorize as "normal."
If this pair of shoes contains the Golden Hide, it's not obvious. The price looks comparatively low, too.

texts.text: I have. When we were young, Xichun would find pretty rocks and petals and gift them to me. I'd keep those hidden in the flower pots at Yihongyuan.

texts.text: Haha... Though this be not a tale of mine, I know that Nicolina had always hidden a key of hers in one of the flower pots decorating the front gates of our castle.
